opening: Punk and post-punk focus, week 2 of 4: Texas punk tonight. Halloween post-punk Oct. 29, D.C. hardcore Nov. 5.
Fontaines D.C. released Dopamine Chamber last Friday, Oct. 16, on XL. Produced by James Ford, 11 tracks. Set 3 plays one of them, Happy For You.
New and loud: Westside Cowboy of Manchester (Island, debut It Goes On out Aug. 21) and Royal Blood, Ten Over Ten, the lead single from Dead Company (Warner, due Nov. 13).
New Rose by The Damned turns 50 tonight. Triple Shot opens Hour 2.
after_texas_set: Dallas first: Nervebreakers, My Girlfriend Is a Rock, from the 1978 Politics EP on Wild Child Records. Loco Gringos, also Dallas, released their only album after singer Tom Foote died in 1990.

Scratch Acid formed in Austin. Greatest Gift is from their 1984 self-titled EP, collected on The Greatest Gift (Touch and Go, 1991). David Yow sang for them, then fronted The Jesus Lizard. Monkey Trick is from Goat (Touch and Go, 1991).
Butthole Surfers came out of San Antonio. Pepper is from Electriclarryland (1996). Big Boys were an Austin band; Fun Fun Fun is a 1982 EP.
after_fontaines: Dopamine Chamber is the band's fifth album and the second with James Ford. Happy For You debuted live at Leeds Festival on Aug. 29.
Two songs from it, Tongue (shit x10) and Japan (fuck x3, shit x3), stay off the air. Their Europe and UK tour started in Lisbon on Oct. 21 (verify).
end_hour_1: Reviewed this month and in rotation: Twisted Teens (two albums), Lex Walton, Yard Act, Little Barrie, Palace, Sluice, This Is Lorelei, Dread Spectre Council, Tricky, Ty Segall.
This Is Lorelei twice: the album track, then MJ Lenderman's version of Dancing in the Club (2025, Double Double Whammy). Radio edit: confirm by ear.
Station ID at the top of the hour.
triple_shot_intro: Thursday Triple Shot: The Damned. New Rose, Oct. 22, 1976, Stiff Records, Nick Lowe producing. The B-side was a fast cover of the Beatles' Help!
Neat Neat Neat is from the first UK punk album (1977). Love Song is from Machine Gun Etiquette (1979).
bay_area_break: Fri. Oct. 23: Cheekface with BODEGA at Cornerstone in Berkeley; Frightwig at Chapel in San Francisco; Protomartyr at The Ritz in San Jose; Julia Jacklin at the Castro (sold out).
Black Flag with Greg Ginn: Fri. Oct. 23 at Felton Music Hall and Sun. Oct. 25 at Cornerstone in Berkeley. Slow Pulp at the Fillmore Wed. Oct. 28.
after_machines: Numbers is from Kraftwerk's Computer World (1981). Nag, Nag, Nag is Cabaret Voltaire's 1979 Rough Trade single. Bauhaus released The Passion of Lovers in June 1981 on Beggars Banquet; it is on Mask.
Consolidated are from San Francisco: Friendly Fascism is the title track of their 1991 Nettwerk album, recorded at Razor's Edge in the city. Fujiya & Miyagi's New Shiny Object is out Oct. 30.
anniversary: Pulp released We Love Life on Oct. 22, 2001, produced by Scott Walker (25 years today; no Pulp track tonight, since The Trees came off the Air Order).

The Avalanches' No Bad Memories came out Oct. 16 with Karen O on Blue Shadows. Stef Chura's Sweet Sweet Midnight is from Midnight (Saddle Creek, 2019); Will Toledo of Car Seat Headrest produced the album and plays on it.
after_heavy_set: Dumb, from Vancouver: Pull Me Up is from Pray 4 Tomorrow (Mint, 2022).
Last stretch is new and loud: Queens of the Stone Age, Insignificant Other, from Perfecth (Matador, out Oct. 30).
Jozef Van Wissem and Jim Jarmusch, Bocca di Lupo and Mouth of the Wolf, Sacred Bones, Nov. 6. Courtney Barnett sings on Never Like You Said.
Eagles of Death Metal cover Careless Whisper on Boots Electric Performing the Best Songs We Never Wrote (2019). Lambrini Girls, Cult of Celebrity, City Slang.
